headline: SILVER BUCKS THE TREND — UP 0.6% TO $58.88 AS GOLD OPENS LOWER ON US-IRAN DAY-2 AIRSTRIKES AND OIL SURGE
snippet: Silver futures opened July 9 at $58.88 per ounce — up 0.6% from Wednesday's close of $58.54 — even as gold remained under pressure at $4,075–$4,112 for a second consecutive day of US military strikes on Iran, which pushed crude oil higher and amplified inflation-rate-hike fears. The gold-silver divergence is becoming structurally notable: silver now sits 52% below its January $121.64 all-time high while gold is 27% below the January $5,589 peak, creating one of the widest gold-silver ratio extremes of the current bull market and setting up the textbook catchup condition that historically precedes silver's highest-returning stretches — when precious metals investors' attention finally rotates from the monetary metal to the industrial.

headline: MINAURUM QUINTERA HITS 1,117 G/T AGEQ OVER 5.95M — 2,557 G/T INNER CORE IN SONORA SILVER VEIN (TSXV:MGG)
source_name: Investing News Network / Minaurum Silver Inc.
snippet: Minaurum Silver (TSXV: MGG) released July 8 assays from four vein zones at the Alamos Silver Project in Sonora, Mexico — with hole AL26-215 cutting 5.95 metres at 1,117 g/t AgEq (including 2.40 metres at 2,557 g/t AgEq) at the Quintera Vein and Europa Sur returning 4.75 metres at 888 g/t AgEq in hole AL26-207. At $59/oz silver, 1,117 g/t AgEq converts to roughly $65.60 per tonne in-situ before recoveries — exceptional economics for a narrow-vein system — and the company is 18 months into a Phase II 50,000-metre resource expansion programme across seven active zones, with an updated resource estimate targeted for H2 2026. The sustained high-grade hits across multiple vein systems demonstrates the Alamos district's consistency rather than a single-hole anomaly.

headline: ANDINA COPPER CONFIRMS THIRD PIUQUENES PORPHYRY IN ARGENTINA — 468M AT 0.50% CU, 164M AT 0.70% CU IN FIRST-EVER HOLE (TSXV:ANDC)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Andina Copper Corp.
snippet: Andina Copper Corp. (TSXV: ANDC) confirmed July 8 that initial drilling at the Piuquenes North target in San Juan, Argentina has intersected a third distinct porphyry copper-gold system within the broader Piuquenes district — hole PIU13 returning 468 metres at 0.50% Cu, 0.30 g/t Au, 3.04 g/t Ag from 700 metres downhole, including a 164-metre higher-grade core at 0.70% Cu, 0.44 g/t Au. Piuquenes North lies immediately north of the Central and East systems already advancing at Andina and is directly adjacent to Aldebaran Resources' Altar copper-gold deposit — one of the largest undeveloped porphyry copper systems in the Americas — placing the discovery in a district that appears to host at least three stacked or coalescing intrusive centres. A 468-metre mineralized intercept in the first discovery hole, in a jurisdiction that has improved materially under Argentina's Milei administration, makes this one of the more consequential new porphyry confirmations reported by a TSX-V junior in 2026.

headline: EAGLE NUCLEAR BREAKS GROUND ON AURORA PFS DRILL — 27,000 FEET AT AMERICA'S LARGEST CONVENTIONAL URANIUM DEPOSIT (NASDAQ:NUCL)
snippet: Eagle Nuclear Energy Corp. (NASDAQ: NUCL) announced July 8 the mobilization of a 47-hole, 27,000-foot diamond drill programme at the Aurora Uranium Project along the Oregon–Nevada border — the largest conventional, measured-and-indicated uranium deposit in the United States, holding 32.75 million pounds indicated and 4.98 million pounds inferred. Two to three rigs will run over an estimated three to four months, with the programme designed to support a Pre-Feasibility Study targeted for H2 2027; newly contracted consultants include BBA USA Inc., SLR International Corporation, and indigenous services firm Yukuskokon Professional Services. For investors tracking the US domestic uranium supply build-out under the current administration's nuclear energy expansion policy, Aurora's scale — sufficient to fuel a 1,000 MW reactor for roughly 30 years — gives NUCL a strategic asset footprint that dwarfs most junior uranium exploration peers.

headline: MIATA METALS PUMA EAST: 17.19M AT 3.14 G/T AU IN FIRST HOLES — NEW GOLD SYSTEM 3KM FROM MAIN SURINAME CORRIDOR (TSXV:MMET)
snippet: Miata Metals Corp. (TSXV: MMET) released July 7 the first drill results from the Puma East target at the Sela Creek Gold Project in Suriname — establishing a significant new discovery 3 kilometres southeast of the advancing Jons Trend–Big Berg corridor, with hole 26DDH-PME-002 returning 17.19 metres at 3.14 g/t Au (including 7.09m at 5.64 g/t Au and 0.90m at 22.8 g/t Au) and hole 26DDH-PME-004 returning 21.64 metres at 1.70 g/t Au. The host rock, structural setting, alteration assemblage, and vein style at Puma East match the defining features of the Jons Trend — suggesting these are co-expressions of a single district-scale orogenic system rather than isolated occurrences. With approximately 12,000 metres completed of a 25,000-metre funded programme and multiple untested targets remaining across the Sela Creek licence area, Miata's discovery inventory continues to grow ahead of any resource delineation.

headline: STILLWATER WEST ADDS THIRD DRILL RIG AND LAUNCHES BIGGEST-EVER PROGRAM — 1.6B LBS NI+CU+CO, 3.8MOZ PGMS, RESOURCE UPDATE DUE (TSXV:PGE)
source_name: Investing News Network / Stillwater Critical Minerals Corp.
snippet: Stillwater Critical Minerals Corp. (TSXV: PGE) announced July 9 the commencement of its largest-ever exploration programme at the Stillwater West project in Montana — expanding to three simultaneous drill rigs and advancing an updated Mineral Resource Estimate now in final stages of independent review. Stillwater West's 2023 MRE defined 1.6 billion pounds of nickel, copper, and cobalt alongside 3.8 million ounces of platinum, palladium, rhodium, and gold — a multi-metal polymetallic resource in a tier-one North American jurisdiction that carries both critical minerals (Ni, Cu) and strategic metals (Pd, Pt, Rh) simultaneously. The updated 2026 MRE will be the first complete re-quantification of Stillwater West's scale since multiple additional drilling campaigns have substantially expanded the resource footprint, making the forthcoming estimate the next material catalyst for the stock.

headline: GOLDGROUP + GOLD RESOURCE GET COURT GREEN LIGHT — 4-MINE MEXICO GOLD-SILVER COMBINATION CLOSES JULY 17 (TSXV:GGA)
source_name: Mexico Business News / Goldgroup Mining Inc.
snippet: Goldgroup Mining (TSXV: GGA) received final BC Supreme Court approval for its US$372 million plan of arrangement with Gold Resource Corporation, targeting a July 17 closing that creates a four-mine, Mexico-focused precious metals producer — spanning the Cerro Prieto mine and San Francisco project in Sonora, the Don David mine in Oaxaca, and the Back Forty project in Michigan. Shareholders voted 99.99% in favour at a July 2 meeting; a post-close 4:1 share consolidation is designed to position the combined company for an NYSE American listing alongside the existing TSX listing. Gold Resource shareholders will hold approximately 40% of the combined entity with Goldgroup retaining 60%, giving the combined group an operational multi-mine footprint and US equity market access that neither company could achieve independently in the current environment.

headline: BATTERY METALS BROADLY RECOVER BUT 3 FACTORS CAP THE RALLY — LFP CHEMISTRY SHIFT, WEAK EV DEMAND, PRICE DESTRUCTION RISK
snippet: Battery metal prices have staged a broad recovery from 2024–2025 lows — lithium carbonate near-tripling from June's CNY 151,750 trough to around CNY 165,000 per tonne, with cobalt and nickel also rebounding — but the rally is supply-constraint-driven rather than demand-driven, and three structural factors limit its sustainability: first, the lithium-iron-phosphate chemistry shift means stationary storage and half of China's EV market use LFP chemistry, which contains neither cobalt nor nickel; second, EV demand is weak on both continents (US down 25% year-on-year after tax credit removal, China off 15%); and third, lithium prices have already reached break-even levels for some grid storage projects, raising demand destruction risk if prices keep rising. For retail investors in battery metals equities, the supply-vs-demand distinction is crucial — a supply-constrained recovery can reverse the moment idled capacity restarts, whereas a demand-driven recovery compounds as adoption accelerates.

headline: GOLDSEEK ELLIOTT WAVE: SILVER'S WAVE IV POSSIBLY DONE AT $55.62 — OIL AND GOLD ALSO NEARING KEY TURNS, GOING LONG
snippet: GoldSeek contributor Gary Kalynchuk (Captain Ewave) published a technical Elliott Wave analysis arguing that silver's multi-month wave iv correction may have completed at the $55.62 low and that oil and gold are simultaneously approaching inflection points where the structural bull trend should reassert — with Kalynchuk establishing fresh long positions backed by put-option stops. His alternate wave count for gold places the $3,959 level as a potential wave (iv) completion point, consistent with gold's current recovery from the $4,030 low toward $4,112. For retail investors trying to time entries in junior silver and gold miners, an Elliott Wave practitioner flagging a potentially completed corrective pattern provides a specific structural reference — the $55.62 silver level must hold as the key invalidation point for the bullish interpretation — more actionable than a generic macro call.

headline: GDX +3.1%, GDXJ +2.8% AS GOLD FELL A SECOND WEEK — POSITIVE MINER-METAL DIVERGENCE SIGNALS POTENTIAL SECTOR RERATING
snippet: Gold mining equities continued to decouple positively from the underlying metal: the VanEck Gold Miners ETF (GDX) advanced 3.1% and the Junior Gold Miners ETF (GDXJ) gained 2.8% during a period when gold fell for a second consecutive week — a positive divergence that historically has preceded sector re-ratings as institutions accumulate depressed miners before the metal price catches up. The GDXJ's MACD turned positive on July 2, 2026 with RSI indicators showing early trend-reversal signals, while producers with renewable energy integration and North American operations are outperforming their diesel-dependent peers exposed to Iran-driven oil costs. For self-directed investors in the junior mining space, relative strength in GDXJ rather than GDX is the more meaningful signal — junior miners carry the highest leverage to any eventual gold price recovery.

headline: WORLD GOLD COUNCIL MID-YEAR 2026: STRUCTURAL BULL SURVIVES H1 OIL SHOCK — CENTRAL BANK BID INTACT, JULY 14 CPI IS THE PIVOT
snippet: The World Gold Council's mid-year 2026 gold outlook, highlighted on GoldSeek, maintains that gold's structural bull market remains intact despite the 28% drawdown from January's $5,589 all-time high — attributing the H1 decline to a specific macro sequence (Iran/Hormuz oil shock → energy inflation → Fed hawkishness repricing) rather than a reversal of the underlying demand fundamentals. The WGC notes that gold has outperformed its historical real-rate sensitivity model throughout the 2025–2026 period, reflecting non-price-elastic demand from central banks (including the PBOC's 20-month buying streak through June) and geopolitical hedgers that rate models alone do not capture. The July 14 US CPI print is identified as the next decisive catalyst: a hotter-than-expected reading reinforces the September rate-hike scenario and near-term headwinds, while a miss unlocks the conditions for the next leg higher in bullion and mining equities.
